Practice · A 78-year-old man with Parkinson disease takes two hours to finish his morning routine, has difficulty fastening buttons, and walks with a shuffling gait. His MMSE is 24 and he pauses before answering. He also reports constipation and blurred vision. His drugs are carbidopa–levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, ropinirole 2 mg three times daily, trihexyphenidyl 2 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at night. Which change addresses the antimuscarinic exposure that Hazzard advises avoiding at his age?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease develops confusion and visual hallucinations after amantadine is added. Which benefit-risk pairing explains why the treatment should be reassessed?

Practice · A 76-year-old woman with Parkinson disease is hospitalized with pneumonia and delirium. She has lost 6 kg in two months because of dysphagia. A video swallow study shows aspiration of thin liquids but safe swallowing of nectar-thick liquids. Her family requests a feeding tube. She takes carbidopa/levodopa, pramipexole, and quetiapine 50 mg at bedtime; MoCA during admission is 18/30. Which principle supports considering speech-therapy-guided, supervised thickened liquids?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease develops progressive dysphagia over three weeks. Meals take 30 minutes, and he has lost 4 kg. He takes levodopa/carbidopa, rasagiline, amantadine, and quetiapine 50 mg at bedtime for hallucinations. Examination shows masked facies, resting tremor, and saliva pooling. A modified barium swallow shows delayed pharyngeal transit with residue; creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which statement explains why increasing dopaminergic medication need not improve his swallowing?

Practice · A man with Parkinson disease is hospitalized for pneumonia. He develops new confusion and hallucinations and has a positive CAM assessment. He is calm, accepts treatment, and is not endangering himself or others. Which initial approach is appropriate?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with mild parkinsonism and type 2 diabetes has six months of worsening short-stepped gait and difficulty initiating movement, without tremor. MRI shows enlarged ventricles and periventricular white-matter changes. Carbidopa-levodopa provides little benefit. CSF opening pressure is 180 mm H2O. In Hazzard’s differential of parkinsonism, which diagnosis is specifically associated with the enlarged-ventricle finding?
Practice · Which FDA-approved drug extends survival and delays the need for ventilation in ALS?

Practice · An 86-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease is hospitalized with aspiration pneumonia. She is bedbound, needs a pureed diet, and has lost 15 lb over three months. She takes carbidopa–levodopa, quetiapine 25 mg at bedtime for hallucinations, and mirtazapine 15 mg for depression; creatinine clearance is 32 mL/min. After stabilization, her daughter asks about tube feeding. The patient and family choose comfort-focused care, and the attending physician and hospice medical director certify a terminal prognosis of less than six months if the illness follows its expected course. Which service model fits these established goals and eligibility?
Practice · A patient with Parkinson disease develops hallucinations and confusion while receiving dopaminergic therapy. Which medication strategy is described by Hazzard?
Practice · A patient with Parkinson disease develops compulsive sexual behavior after an increase in a dopamine agonist dose. Which medication change targets the described adverse effect?
Practice · A man with longstanding Parkinson disease who takes dopaminergic medication develops orthostatic hypotension. Which interpretation matches Hazzard?

Practice · A person with Parkinson disease responds well to each levodopa dose, but stiffness and slowness recur before each daytime dose. There is no significant dyskinesia. The initial plan is to adjust the timing of the existing formulation. Which change addresses this end-of-dose problem?
Practice · An older woman with Parkinson disease receives amantadine to reduce dyskinesias. Which adverse effect explains difficulty tolerating the drug in older adults according to Hazzard?

Practice · A 91-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, dysphagia requiring a pureed diet, and recurrent aspiration pneumonia has severe constipation. He takes carbidopa/levodopa, pramipexole, and lansoprazole. He spends an hour straining on the toilet. Examination shows normal anal tone but impaired coordination of pelvic floor relaxation. Lactulose, suppositories, and enemas have not helped. His creatinine clearance is 35 mL/min. Which intervention directly targets the pelvic floor coordination problem?

Practice · An 83-year-old woman with Parkinson disease, depression and overactive bladder develops confusion and visual hallucinations. She takes carbidopa–levodopa, pramipexole, nortriptyline and solifenacin. Which medication pair contributes the greatest anticholinergic burden?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with Parkinson disease becomes confused during admission for pneumonia. He takes carbidopa–levodopa, rasagiline and pramipexole. Compared with levodopa, which complication occurs more often with dopamine agonists in older patients?
Practice · A patient with bradykinesia is being assessed for Parkinson disease. Which interpretation of an adjunctive finding is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 75-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia has Parkinson disease, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and insomnia. He takes carbidopa-levodopa, tamsulosin, and zolpidem. He develops acute confusion and visual hallucinations, with a positive CAM screen despite stable vital signs and no fever. Which recommendation about zolpidem agrees with the 2023 Beers Criteria?
Practice · A hospitalized patient with Parkinson disease requires a medication change because of adverse effects. Which complication does Hazzard associate with abrupt withdrawal of levodopa?

Practice · An 85-year-old man with mild Parkinson disease and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22) develops visual hallucinations and paranoid delusions. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg twice daily and pramipexole 0.5 mg three times daily. Vital signs and head CT are normal. Which medication-review conclusion follows Hazzard's comparison of dopamine agonists with levodopa?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with Parkinson disease (Hoehn-Yahr stage 3) is hospitalized after a backward fall with head injury; CT shows no acute finding. On day two his MoCA is 22/30, compared with 25/30 three months earlier. He is more confused in the evening and sees children in the room. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily and pramipexole 1 mg three times daily. Alongside evaluation for acute causes, which medication-review approach addresses a recognized contributor to hallucinations?

Practice · During hospitalization of an 83-year-old man with Parkinson disease, abrupt discontinuation of levodopa is considered. Which complication is the explicit reason Hazzard gives for avoiding sudden withdrawal?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman develops a poorly controlled right arm over one year. She drops objects, and the arm sometimes grasps her clothes involuntarily. She has difficulty planning meals and operating the microwave. Examination shows asymmetric right-arm rigidity and dystonia, cortical sensory loss, and ideomotor apraxia. MRI shows asymmetric left frontoparietal atrophy. Six months of carbidopa-levodopa has not helped. Which clinical syndrome best describes this combination?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease has persistent cognitive decline after reversible acute and medication-related contributors have been excluded. The current goal is to treat cognitive symptoms. Which medication class is described in Hazzard as useful for this goal?

Practice · An 89-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease develops rigidity and fever after running out of carbidopa-levodopa and stopping it abruptly. Which medication change is the recognized trigger of a neuroleptic malignant-like syndrome described by Hazzard?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, hypertension and osteoarthritis is assessed after a fall in assisted living. He takes carbidopa/levodopa, amlodipine and as-needed acetaminophen. Examination shows masked facies and cogwheel rigidity, with a marked fall in blood pressure and dizziness on standing. Which approach fits the described treatment principles for orthostatic hypotension?

Practice · A person with dementia with Lewy bodies has recovered from a severe reaction to haloperidol. The patient is now stable but still has visual hallucinations and has not received cognitive treatment. Which drug trial is described by Hazzard as having the potential to reduce hallucinations in this condition?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with longstanding Parkinson disease develops cognitive decline and visual hallucinations while taking carbidopa-levodopa, ropinirole, and amantadine. During medication review, which description of amantadine is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 85-year-old man with Parkinson disease and recurrent falls freezes when walking through doorways. He takes carbidopa-levodopa and quetiapine for hallucinations. Examination shows a shuffling gait, reduced arm swing, and difficulty with tandem walking. Which advice about physical therapy and cueing follows Hazzard?

Practice · A 79-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease and recurrent UTIs has worsening constipation despite lactulose 30 mL daily. She has had no bowel movement for five days and reports abdominal pain. Examination shows abdominal distension and a large, firm rectal fecal impaction. She takes carbidopa/levodopa, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and prophylactic trimethoprim; creatinine clearance is 35 mL/min. Before inserting rectal enemas or suppositories, what does Hazzard recommend for the firm impaction?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, orthostatic hypotension, and recurrent falls is admitted after syncope. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/250 mg four times daily, midodrine 10 mg three times daily, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily, and tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily for BPH. Blood pressure falls from 130/80 to 88/54 on standing. His Clinical Frailty Scale score is 8/9. His daughter asks about prognosis and says he wished to avoid being kept alive by machines. Which approach to tamsulosin follows Hazzard's management of orthostatic hypotension?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, BPH, and insomnia reports dizziness on standing and three falls in the past month. He takes carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, terazosin 5 mg at bedtime, zolpidem 10 mg nightly, and recently added oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily. Blood pressure falls from 145/85 supine to 118/70 standing with dizziness. Which pair combines a nonselective peripheral alpha-1 blocker with a strongly anticholinergic drug in Beers 2023?

Practice · An 84-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease has severe REM sleep behavior disorder, with punching and kicking that have injured staff. Clonazepam 0.5 mg and melatonin 12 mg have not helped. He needs full ADL assistance, and his wife reports increased confusion on treatment. Levodopa was recently increased for rigidity. Which approach addresses symptom burden and treatment goals together?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with major depression, Parkinson disease, and mild cognitive impairment has not responded to several antidepressant trials. After gradual titration over several weeks, pramipexole reaches 0.5 mg three times daily in addition to mirtazapine 30 mg nightly; he also takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg and entacapone 200 mg three times daily. Two days later, his wife reports new online gambling and inappropriate sexual comments. Which recognized dopamine-agonist adverse effect best matches these behaviors?

Practice · An 86-year-old man with Parkinson disease, BPH and recurrent falls takes carbidopa–levodopa, tamsulosin, oxybutynin and mirtazapine. He has dry mouth, severe constipation, hesitancy and a postvoid residual of 250 mL. Which medication change best addresses this combination?

Practice · A man with Parkinson disease has recurrent rigidity before each levodopa dose, followed by a good response and no peak-dose dyskinesia. The team plans to alter the frequency of the same formulation before adding a drug. Which change fits wearing-off?

Practice · An 85-year-old man is in a nursing facility for rehabilitation after a hip fracture. He has Parkinson disease and benign prostatic hyperplasia and takes carbidopa/levodopa, tamsulosin, oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed, and ferrous sulfate. He has had no bowel movement for 7 days despite daily lactulose. Abdominal radiography shows a moderate colonic stool burden, and creatinine clearance is 38 mL/min. Which option is supported for ongoing laxative treatment?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, depression, and chronic pain from spinal stenosis attends a medication review. His wife reports increasing daytime sedation and two near-falls. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, tramadol 50 mg four times daily, and docusate 100 mg twice daily. He also takes oral diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Which characteristic of diphenhydramine explains the Beers recommendation to avoid this use?

Practice · An 85-year-old man is found on the kitchen floor after preparing breakfast, with no memory of the collapse. He has Parkinson disease, BPH, hypertension, and chronic back pain. He takes carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 mg four times daily, tamsulosin 0.8 mg nightly, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and tramadol 50 mg as needed. Examination shows resting tremor and bradykinesia. Which pairing correctly describes two recognized contributors to orthostatic hypotension present in this history?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with advanced Parkinson disease, depression, and recurrent urinary tract infections attends follow-up. She lives in assisted living, uses a wheelchair, and has mild dysphagia. Her daughter reports worsening tremor and two falls this month. Medicines are carbidopa-levodopa 25/250 mg four times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, and nitrofurantoin 100 mg daily for prophylaxis. Her creatinine clearance is 28 mL/min. Which statement about nitrofurantoin follows Beers 2023?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with Parkinson disease is found confused and nearly unresponsive. Temperature is 32.5 degrees C, blood pressure 90/55, and heart rate 48. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg four times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, benztropine 1 mg twice daily, and chlorpromazine 50 mg at bedtime for chronic hiccups. Recent TSH is 4.2 and creatinine 1.8; ECG shows J waves. Rewarming has begun. Which explanation warrants a medication review while rewarming continues?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with Parkinson disease develops visual hallucinations during dopaminergic treatment. Acute contributors have been assessed, and the team suspects a medication contribution. Which medication-review approach does Hazzard describe?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with Parkinson disease and REM sleep behavior disorder is hospitalized after his wife calls emergency services. He struck her during sleep, causing a black eye. He is distressed, has no waking history of violence, and wants to remain at home; his wife requests nursing-home placement for safety. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily and ropinirole 2 mg at bedtime. Which statement about the source’s approach to this sleep disorder is correct?

Practice · An 83-year-old man with Parkinson disease has repeated falls when turning and freezes at doorways despite carbidopa/levodopa and rasagiline. Examination shows masked facies, cogwheel rigidity and multiple small steps when turning. Which rehabilitation approach is supported for freezing of gait?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease and knee osteoarthritis has recurrent falls and dizziness on standing, including two falls while reaching for his walker. He takes carbidopa–levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, and celecoxib 200 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 138/82 supine to 106/68 standing with dizziness. There is a moderate knee effusion. Which consideration supports reviewing the pramipexole dose as part of management?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman who has never smoked has stage IV lung adenocarcinoma, brain metastases, and an EGFR L858R mutation. She takes amlodipine, metformin, and simvastatin, has reduced renal function, and lives independently but has stopped driving because of mild cognitive impairment. Which initial treatment is supported by the FLAURA results described in Hazzard, including improved overall survival and efficacy in CNS metastases?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman has chronic dizziness and recurrent falls, with persistent imbalance worsened by head movement. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, simvastatin 40 mg, and meclizine 25 mg three times daily for three months. She has no nystagmus, a normal Romberg test, difficulty with tandem gait, and negative orthostatic measurements. Which strategy follows Hazzard's approach to prolonged vestibular-suppressant use and chronic dizziness?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman living alone in a two-story home has fallen three times in two weeks. She says she simply tripped. MMSE is 28/30, gait speed 0.7 m/s, tandem walking is impaired, and Romberg testing is positive. Vision is 20/40 in both eyes with cataracts. She takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Vitamin B12 is 180 pg/mL (laboratory lower limit 200); folate and TSH are normal. Which approach addresses the range of risk factors through a multifactorial falls-prevention plan?
Practice · An older patient develops muscle pain while taking a statin. The CK level is 12 times the upper limit of normal. Which action concerning the statin is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with advanced chronic kidney disease, coronary artery disease, and recently diagnosed colon cancer has severe constipation and cramping abdominal pain after chemotherapy. He takes ondansetron, aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol. Vital signs are stable; the abdomen is distended with hyperactive bowel sounds, and abdominal imaging shows fecal loading without obstruction. Which laxative does Hazzard advise against because of its greater adverse-effect risk in older adults?
Practice · An older woman taking a statin develops muscle pain and a CK level 12 times the upper limit of normal. Which action regarding the statin is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 24) and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73 m²) is hospitalized with pneumonia. On day three she develops acute confusion, visual hallucinations, and agitation; the CAM is positive. She pulls at an indwelling urinary catheter that is no longer medically needed. She is receiving levofloxacin, acetaminophen, amlodipine, and atorvastatin. Which initial intervention best follows Hazzard’s nonpharmacologic approach?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with diabetes and mild cognitive impairment has lost about 7 kg in four months. He takes small bites, chews extensively, reports food going 'the wrong way,' and has a wet, gurgly voice after meals. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily; creatinine clearance is 44 mL/min. Modified barium swallow shows vallecular residue and delayed swallow initiation. Which statement correctly characterizes rehabilitative swallowing therapy considered after this assessment?

Practice · A 75-year-old man with recently diagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism (initial TSH 8.2) returns after eight weeks of levothyroxine 25 micrograms daily. He feels more energetic and again walks his dog daily, but his wife reports new evening confusion. TSH is 2.8, free T4 is 1.3 ng/dL, and temperature is 36.8 degrees C. His medications include levothyroxine, atorvastatin 40 mg, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Which statement about diphenhydramine supports reviewing its use in this patient?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with coronary artery disease and a previous myocardial infarction takes a high-intensity statin. She tolerates it well and has good functional status. Which approach is appropriate according to Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 22) presents after 3 days of productive cough, fever and delirium. He has fallen twice that day and missed medications. His usual drugs are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Temperature is 38.8°C, BP 95/60 mmHg, pulse 110/min, respiratory rate 28/min and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. Chest radiography shows right lower-lobe consolidation; WBC is 16.2, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.2) and glucose 340 mg/dL. Oxygenation and hemodynamic support are being addressed. Which infection-directed strategy accords with Hazzard while microbiology results are pending?
Practice · A 79-year-old woman has had a myocardial infarction and can tolerate statin therapy. Which goal of intensive lipid-lowering therapy in this period is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, stage 3 CKD (eGFR 45), and recent functional decline is scheduled for MitraClip placement. She now uses a walker and her daughter manages her medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin. She is anxious about general anesthesia. Which procedural plan is described in Hazzard?

Practice · A 72-year-old man reports worsening urinary frequency, nocturia four to five times nightly, and a weak stream for six months. His AUASI is 18. He has hypertension, diabetes, and recent falls, takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin, and lives alone. Which drug treats BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms through selective alpha-1A blockade?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman is brought by her daughter for routine follow-up. She has fallen twice in the past month and seems more forgetful. She lives alone and manages her finances, but recently burned a pot while cooking. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amitriptyline 50 mg at night for neuropathic pain, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/65 after three minutes standing. Her Mini-Cog score is 2/5. Which approach to amitriptyline addresses the medication concern identified in Beers 2023?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman reports dizziness when wearing high-necked sweaters or adjusting necklaces. Yesterday she briefly lost consciousness during hair washing at a salon. She has coronary artery disease treated with stenting and hypertension, and takes aspirin 81 mg daily, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. If contraindications are excluded, which test directly evaluates suspected carotid sinus hypersensitivity?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment, diabetes, and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52) reports chronic constipation at her annual visit. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and pravastatin 20 mg daily. Increasing fiber and fluids has not helped. Her daughter reports recent use of ibuprofen 400 mg daily for joint pain. Examination and CBC are normal. Which statement about ibuprofen and constipation follows Hazzard's discussion of NSAIDs?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with stable coronary disease, diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) had his last myocardial infarction three years ago. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metformin 1000 mg twice daily. LDL is 72 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.8%. His wife reports missed evening doses. Which prescribing approach directly addresses the regimen-complexity problem described by Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old man has frailty with unintentional 15-lb weight loss, exhaustion, weakness, and slow walking speed, and stage 3b CKD (eGFR 36). He takes 12 medications, including atorvastatin 80 mg, aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 40 mg. Blood pressure is 108/64 and albumin 3.1. Which approach follows Hazzard's principles for reviewing this medication burden?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, coronary artery disease, and depression presents with dizziness and weakness. He takes metformin, atorvastatin, metoprolol 100 mg twice daily, lisinopril, paroxetine 40 mg daily, and recently added amitriptyline 75 mg for neuropathy. BP is 102/68 seated and 84/52 standing, heart rate is 58, and QTc is 492 ms. Which assessment of amitriptyline follows from the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?

Practice · An older patient develops delirium after admission for myocardial infarction and coronary catheterization. Several medications were started together. Which approach to evaluating medication contributions follows Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with a myocardial infarction 12 years ago, chronic stable angina, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease attends a medication review. He functions well and walks two miles daily without symptoms. He takes aspirin 81 mg, metoprolol 50 mg twice daily, amlodipine 5 mg, and atorvastatin 40 mg. Blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg, heart rate is 64 beats/min, and a recent echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 55%. Before deciding whether to deprescribe metoprolol, which finding would support deprescribing under Hazzard's framework?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and mild dementia has weight loss and frequent falls. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, and aspirin 81 mg. BMI fell from 23 to 19 over 8 months; HbA1c is 6.4% and LDL is 68. She forgets meals and struggles with cooking. Grip strength is 14 kg, and she rises slowly while holding furniture. Which adjustment addresses the hypoglycemia risk emphasized by Hazzard?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman without known atherosclerotic disease is being assessed before a decision about statin therapy for primary prevention. She has mild cognitive decline. Which approach reflects the uncertainty described in Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment develops fatigue, difficulty shopping and a postural blood-pressure fall after starting amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. She also takes metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin. Which change best addresses the new symptoms?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman falls during cardiac rehabilitation after CABG. She takes a high-dose statin, has reduced kidney function, and has proximal muscle weakness on examination. Which listed test measures a muscle enzyme used in evaluating suspected myopathy?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman attending a new-patient visit reports occasional urinary leakage but is embarrassed to discuss it. Her daughter reports daily laundry and a urine odor in the apartment. She takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Examination is normal apart from mild vulvar redness, and postvoid residual is 85 mL. During medication review, which approach to diphenhydramine is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with peripheral arterial disease and intermittent claudication remains limited in walking despite supervised exercise. She takes an antiplatelet agent and a statin, has no heart failure, and is not currently scheduled for a vascular intervention. Which additional recommendation is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18) is brought to the emergency department after two days of unusual behavior. His daughter recalls an unnamed constipation medicine. He is confused and has asterixis. Results are sodium 138, potassium 4.1, creatinine 1.4, and magnesium 4.8 mEq/L (laboratory reference range 1.5–2.5). His other medications are donepezil, memantine, and atorvastatin. Which statement about laxative safety supports investigating magnesium hydroxide exposure?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman has peripheral arterial disease (ABI 0.45), stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22), and a recent fall with hip fracture. Claudication now limits walking to 50 feet, and duplex shows 80% superficial femoral artery stenosis. She takes clopidogrel 75 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. When planning exercise within her safe capabilities, which walking approach is described for claudication?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman has recurrent near-syncope when rising from a chair after recently starting doxazosin 4 mg nightly for hypertension. Blood pressure is 158/78 supine and 122/68 after three minutes standing, with pulse rising from 68 to 74. Her daughter reports two falls this month and refusal to shower alone. She also takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Which medication-review approach follows the Beers recommendation for doxazosin used as an antihypertensive?

Practice · An 85-year-old man without known cardiovascular disease, with mild cognitive decline and falls, is referred for consideration of a statin for primary prevention. Which approach is consistent with Hazzard?

Practice · A relatively healthy 78-year-old man has no prior cardiovascular event, an LDL-C of 148 mg/dL, independent function and an estimated life expectancy exceeding five years. Which approach to primary-prevention statin treatment follows the discussion in Hazzard?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes and stage 3a chronic kidney disease is hospitalized for pneumonia. On the third day he develops new confusion, difficulty following commands and picking at the sheets; his wife reports that he was cognitively clear the day before. Medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, ceftriaxone and as-needed diphenhydramine for sleep. Which approach fits the medication component of delirium management?

Practice · A 78-year-old man has type 2 diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and stage 3 CKD (eGFR 45 mL/min). He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg daily, lisinopril 40 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, tiotropium, and simvastatin 20 mg daily. He reports two falls on standing in the past month; HbA1c is 7.2%, and blood pressure falls from 128/76 sitting to 108/68 standing. Separate evaluation of the falls is planned. Which medication change best reduces hypoglycemia risk in this patient?

Practice · A 66-year-old woman received high-dose influenza vaccine in October. In March she asks about waning antibodies. She has diabetes and hypertension, takes an ACE inhibitor and a statin, and had no adverse vaccine reaction. Which statement accurately explains the influenza-vaccination recommendation described in Hazzard?
